comparison: Both address claims C73-C75 about inactivating mutations abolishing transport and fluorescence. OpenEval finds this provides 'strong evidence' that fluorescence reports transport-related conformational changes (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers acknowledge the data but express uncertainty, noting it 'would require more information on binding and how this might be differentiated in the mutants' (UNCERTAIN).

Both evaluate claims C77-C80 about the suppressor screen linking transport and fluorescence. OpenEval considers this 'strong' genetic evidence supporting that fluorescence reports transport (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers see potential value but state it 'would require more information on binding' to be definitive (UNCERTAIN). Peer review also includes C81-C82 about Km variants.

Both address sensor characterization (C8, C9, C64-C69). OpenEval finds 'comprehensive characterization' with electrophysiology confirming transport kinetics are preserved (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers acknowledge sensors 'convincingly show' fluorescence changes with extracellular NH4+ but express major concern that data 'do not seem to differentiate ammonium binding and transport' (UNCERTAIN). Peer review encompasses broader claims including C53-C55, C100-C101.

OpenEval R1 addresses sensor construction (C7, C53, C58-C60, C63) and finds it well-documented (SUPPORTED). Peer R1 includes C7, C53, C63 among broader characterization claims but focuses uncertainty on whether sensors report transport versus binding rather than construction success.

Both address claims C54-C55, C100-C101 about sensor interpretation and limitations. OpenEval views the acknowledgment of limitations (inability to distinguish binding from transport) as appropriate given the data (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers emphasize this same limitation as a major concern, stating they are 'not at all convinced that the signal reports transport activity' (UNCERTAIN).

Both address generalizability claims C83-C86 about AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac. OpenEval finds Figure 9 data supports that the design principle applies to related transporters (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept the successful creation of additional sensors, describing work as 'convincing' (SUPPORTED). Strong agreement on this technical achievement.

Both address sensor optimization (C70-C72). OpenEval finds the screening of ~350 variants and identification of improved sensors demonstrates systematic improvement (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers do not question the optimization process, implicitly accepting it as part of work described as 'convincing, satisfying, and carefully done' (SUPPORTED). Strong agreement.

Both address claims C61-C62 about initial negative results and linker optimization rationale. OpenEval accepts this as appropriate motivation for systematic screening (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept the optimization methodology without question (SUPPORTED). Agreement on methodological approach.

Both address mechanistic conclusions about conformational changes (C96-C97, C117-C118). OpenEval finds evidence for conformational changes during transport while acknowledging uncertainty about precise steps (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers challenge this interpretation, stating 'the inference that the channels...must change conformation requires the assumption' and note fluorescence 'seems to be a protonation change and not necessarily a conformational change' (UNCERTAIN).

Both address structural/mechanistic background (C112-C116). OpenEval finds this accurately summarizes prior work and provides context for conformational change interpretation (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question whether conformational changes are actually demonstrated, suggesting protonation changes upon binding could explain the signal without conformational changes (UNCERTAIN).

Both address technological advance and applications (C10-C11, C94-C95). OpenEval finds the demonstrated capabilities support the claimed advantages (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers acknowledge sensors as 'an important technical advance' for tracking extracellular NH4+ but emphasize they are 'not at all convinced that the signal reports transport activity' versus binding (UNCERTAIN). Peer review also addresses C92-C93, C121, C126.

OpenEval R5 addresses C81-C82 about Km variants showing ~100-fold difference, finding this demonstrates successful engineering of altered substrate affinity (SUPPORTED). Peer R4 addresses C77-C82 including the Km variants within the suppressor screen context, expressing uncertainty about distinguishing binding from transport.

OpenEval R19 addresses C119-C121 distinguishing current work from prior cpGFP sensors, finding the claim that sensors monitor 'activity states' supported by correlation data despite acknowledged limitations (SUPPORTED). Peer R7 includes C121 and questions whether sensors truly report 'transport activity' versus binding (UNCERTAIN).

OpenEval R21 addresses C126-C130 about main achievements and future applications, finding C126 well-supported and C127-C130 appropriate speculation (SUPPORTED). Peer R7 includes C126 but emphasizes uncertainty about what the sensors actually measure.

OpenEval R11 addresses C57 about AMT1;3 topology prediction used for sensor design. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not question the topology model or insertion site selection strategy.

OpenEval R13 addresses C98, C125 about future structural studies needed to characterize conformational changes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer concerns about conformational versus protonation changes relate to this need.

OpenEval R14 addresses background claims C1-C4, C31, C34-C36 about ammonium transport biology. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not question the background literature or biological context.
OpenEval R15 addresses background claims C37-C44 about Arabidopsis AMTs. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accepted the biological context for choosing AMT1;3.
OpenEval R16 addresses claims C47-C52 about limitations of existing methods. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not dispute the need for new tools.

OpenEval R17 addresses transceptor literature context (C102-C111). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though transceptor concepts relate to peer concerns about distinguishing binding from transport.
OpenEval R20 addresses structural parallels between AMTs and LeuT (C122-C124). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not question these structural comparisons.
OpenEval R22 addresses methodological background claims C5-C6, C12-C21. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not dispute the methodological context.
OpenEval R23 addresses hypothesis and rationale (C22-C30) based on cpGFP sensor precedents. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accepted the design rationale.
OpenEval R24 addresses background on mammalian and yeast transporters (C32-C33, C45-C46). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not question this background.
OpenEval R25 addresses biosensor applications background (C87-C91). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not dispute the broader biosensor context.

Peer R6 addresses mechanistic interpretation claims including C96-C97, C112-C118 with major uncertainty about whether conformational changes versus protonation changes explain the signal. OpenEval addresses these claims separately in R8 (C96-C97, C117-C118) and R18 (C112-C116), both finding them supported with appropriate caveats.
